**v1.14.0: in carry mode the main wizard now plays its own hand (or blades or heals the carry), Alt+M picks which Wizard101 window the bot plays, and Setup can install any version.**

None of this has been tried in the game yet. Watch debug.log the first few carry-mode battles.

- **Carry mode: the main wizard plays too.**
  - **Before:** in carry mode (Alt+K, two clients on one PC) the main wizard passed every round and the carry fought alone.
  - **Now:** each round the main plays first, then the carry.
  - **What the main does** is a new setting, Settings > TWO CLIENTS ON ONE PC (`carrymain`):
    - **Plays its own hand** (the default): its own cards, deck and school, as the bot plays any wizard.
    - **Blader:** its blades and traps go on the carry, using the party code's Blader part with the carry as the hitter. It hits only for a kill or with nothing else to do.
    - **Healer:** heals whichever of the two is lowest under "Heal under this %", else boosts the carry as a Blader.
    - **Passes:** the old way - the carry fights alone. **Pick this to keep carry mode as it was.**
  - **Each wizard's battle is its own:** the blades and traps it cast, its planned hit, its deck, its round count and its name plate are kept aside while the other plays.
  - **Names from each client's memory:** both clients write the one game log, so the log can't tell the two wizards apart. In carry mode the bot also no longer notes a character's school from the log.
  - **Not handled yet:**
    - As Blader or Healer, the main hits in a battle's first round: the carry's name is read in the round it first plays.
    - The carry's kill check doesn't count the main's blades, so it may hit a round sooner than it needs to.
    - With a party across PCs as well, the main's boosts go to the carry only.
- **New: Alt+M - the main Wizard101 window.**
  - **How:** click into the Wizard101 window the bot should play and press Alt+M. Alt+M in it again: back to the window in front, as before. The key can be changed on the dashboard's Keys tab.
  - **What it does:** every window the bot finds, brings up, measures or clicks is that one's, and the helper reads its memory. Other Wizard101 windows are left alone.
  - **Reconnects:** a reconnect closes and restarts only that client. If its game closes, nothing else is played meanwhile; the next Wizard101 started becomes the main.
  - **Carry mode** takes the picked window as the main, so switching carry mode off and on to swap them isn't needed any more.
- **New: Setup's Version list.**
  - **The list:** Setup.exe shows this folder's version, then every release on GitHub, newest first. No token is needed.
  - **Installing one:** Install with another version picked downloads it and puts it in as an update does, keeping your settings, learned cards and routes. It goes into your Programs folder when "Install to your Programs folder" is ticked, else into Setup's own folder. Never into a git checkout (it suggests `git checkout <tag>`).
  - **Going back to an older version:** asked first, and that install's auto-update is turned off - the bot would otherwise put the newest back within minutes. Picking the latest again turns it back on as it was.
  - **Download only:** alpha-v1 (the original 2018 AutoFarmer, AutoHotkey v1.1) and v0.02-v0.06 are unpacked into your Downloads folder, not installed.
  - **The updater:** a download GitHub refuses with your saved token (an expired one) is tried once more without it.
- **Checked:** the five release scripts load, and 884 of 885 vision tests pass, including 4 new ones for carry mode (`test_ahk_names`' speedhack path test errors, as on v1.12.0). Each wizard's battle being kept apart was run with test values. Setup's version list was run hidden against the real releases in scratch folders; its window hasn't been looked at on screen yet.
- **Updating:** the updater offers this to every install. Your settings, learned cards, routes and recorded battles are kept. A copy run from the code: git pull.
